title: Run crash new WinUI3 Keyboard Manager Editor on Windows Server 2022

judgment.rationale: The event-viewer crash signature matches the WinUI 3 Keyboard Manager editor startup family already fixed by PR #49524.
evidence: The issue body includes an Application Error event for PowerToys.KeyboardManagerEditorUI.exe faulting in Microsoft.UI.Input.dll with exception code 0xc0000409.
That matches the same WinUI 3 Keyboard Manager editor launch-crash family investigated in related issue #49399 and issue #49434.
Merged PR #49524 explicitly fixed the new Keyboard Manager editor by building it self-contained to avoid mixed Windows App SDK provenance at startup.
The issue contains no conflicting newer comments or linked alternative fix path.
judgment.recommended_action: Handle this with the existing self-contained editor fix path and current-build retesting rather than opening a separate Server 2022-specific editor crash design.

fix_assessment.rationale: A merged upstream fix already targets this startup crash signature directly.

issue_context.summary: Opening the new WinUI 3 Keyboard Manager editor on Windows Server 2022 crashes in Microsoft.UI.Input.dll with 0xc0000409. That signature aligns with the self-contained packaging fix already merged in PR #49524.
known_information: The issue targets Keyboard Manager on PowerToys 0.100.2 installed via WinGet on Windows Server 2022.
The body includes a full Application Error event log entry naming Microsoft.UI.Input.dll as the faulting module.
The crash happens in the WinUI 3 editor process, not in remap execution or the classic editor path.
There are no public comments, attachments, or competing linked fix paths on the live issue.
inferences: This is part of the same editor-startup dependency family already fixed elsewhere, not evidence of a distinct code path requiring a new design.
Windows Server 2022 is relevant for validation, but not enough on its own to override the existing strong ownership signal from PR #49524.
issue_context.analysis: The issue is specific, but the ownership signal is stronger than the need for new investigation. The lightweight dashboard outcome is to keep this with the known self-contained WinUI 3 editor fix family and avoid spawning a second, platform-specific duplicate investigation.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the full issue body and extracted the crash signature from the included Event Viewer text.
Compared that signature with the known WinUI 3 Keyboard Manager editor crash family and the previously reviewed issue #49434 / #49399 evidence.
Reviewed PR #49524 to confirm it directly addresses the editor-startup packaging problem behind this crash family.
